description: Found building fz-sc8.237. def kind(b) when byte_size(b) > 1, do: byte_size(b) with kind(:a) somewhere is refused at compile time: 'spec/violation: call to byte_size/1 violates its @spec for arguments (:a); the declared domain is (bitstring)', pointing at the body call. Elixir compiles and runs it: byte_size(:a) in the guard fails the clause, so the body never sees :a. A guard function given a value outside its domain makes the guard false (since fz-rs7.4), so the clause body runs only for arguments inside the domain of every guard call that must succeed; the body should be typed with the argument narrowed to that domain, as an is_* guard already narrows. Same for bit_size/1 (fixture 01198 keeps bit_size out of its guarded bodies for this reason). Related: fz-ep5.4 (type predicates recognised from guards), fz-qbh (one admission rule). Done when: an oracle fixture with guarded bodies calling byte_size/bit_size/map_size/tuple_size on the guarded argument, applied to a non-matching value, matches Elixir on interp, run and build.
title: A guard that calls a function narrows its argument to that function's domain for the clause body
